issues.claim: Guard placement as designed: a single new file Molt/AxiomsCertAnchored.lean holds ALL #guard_msgs/#print axioms blocks, including for the two MoltPetit.Model-namespace theorems (keyrot_deep_block_agreement_anchored, keyrot_certified_suffix_agreement_anchored, AcceptedSuffixK.history) that live in the MoltPetit lib, not the Molt lib.
issues.actual: Every other design in this batch that adds both a MoltPetit.Model theorem and a Molt/ wrapper theorem creates a PAIRED set of guard files -- one under MoltPetit/Results/ (guarding the core names, imported from MoltPetit.lean) and one under Molt/ (guarding the paper-namespace names, imported from Molt.lean). Confirmed for W1 (MoltPetit/Results/LockstepCertAxioms.lean + Molt/LockstepCertAxioms.lean), W3a (MoltPetit/Results/AxiomsKeyStealingTimed.lean + Molt/AxiomsSyncRuleTimed.lean), and W5 (MoltPetit/Results/AxiomsLockstepGen.lean + Molt/AxiomsLockstepGen.lean). CLAUDE.md itself names exactly four per-lib audit files (MoltPetit/Results/Axioms.lean, MoltPetit/Custody/Axioms.lean, Rust/Axioms.lean, Molt/Axioms.lean) as what the build enforces axiom-hygiene through. W2's single combined file under Molt/ means the two new core-level theorems are guarded only when Molt is built alongside MoltPetit (true for the repo's own `lake build` / `nix run .#verify-lean`, which build all four libs together, but not for a `lake build MoltPetit`-only invocation, which elaborates MoltPetit.lean's now-added import of the core file but runs no #print axioms check on it). The design itself flags this exact fork as an unresolved open question ('Guard placement: one new file ... or split into MoltPetit/Results/AxiomsCertAnchored.lean + Molt/AxiomsCertAnchored.lean to mirror the existing two-ledger layout?') without resolving it, so the file layout as specified in new_files is the non-conforming variant by default.
issues.fix: Resolve the design's own open question toward the two-ledger split used by W1/W3a/W5: add MoltPetit/Results/AxiomsCertAnchored.lean guarding MoltPetit.Model.keyrot_deep_block_agreement_anchored, MoltPetit.Model.AcceptedSuffixK.history, and MoltPetit.Model.keyrot_certified_suffix_agreement_anchored, imported from MoltPetit.lean (one more additive root-import line, after MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingCertAnchored); keep Molt/AxiomsCertAnchored.lean for the four Molt-namespace theorems/alias only. Both new guard files remain additive-only; touches_existing grows by one line, size estimate is essentially unchanged.

ordering_notes: W2 is genuinely a leaf/root node for build purposes: depends_on is empty and every one of the six items that mention a relationship to W2 (W1 implicitly by omission, W3a, W4, W5 by omission, W6 by omission, W7 by omission) treats it as non-blocking in both directions -- all cross-references found are marked hard=false or are pure shape-similarity notes ('no shared code'). This matches docs/rollout/ROLLOUT_NOTES.md's own sequencing table (W2: '1-2 sessions, cheapest of the three designed; no dependencies'). The only structural friction is administrative, not semantic: five other items (W1, W3a, W5, W6, W7) also append lines to the same two root files (MoltPetit.lean, Molt.lean) that W2 touches, each anchored to a specific 'after line N' insertion point; since Lean import order is not semantically significant, landing these in any order just means later patches must re-locate their anchor line (e.g. W2's 'after MoltPetit.Model.KeyStealingHorizon' remains valid regardless of what W1/W5/W6/W7 insert elsewhere in the same file), so this is a patch-application/merge-conflict detail for whoever lands the items, not a design defect and not a reason to reorder. No structure or definition name is claimed by two items. The one real file-layout deviation (guard-file placement, see issues) is self-disclosed by the design as an open question rather than smuggled in silently.
revised_effort: 1-2 sessions, matching the design's own estimate and docs/rollout/ROLLOUT_NOTES.md's independent table entry ('W2 | 1-2 sessions | cheapest of the three designed; no dependencies'); adopting the guard-file-split fix above adds at most ~15-30 minutes (one more small file plus one more import line), not a session.
